title: Where do the four floors go on the line?
description: Four floors, minus seven, minus four, plus three and minus ten, are marked on the floor line by counting ticks from zero. The marks are checked by reading them from the top to the bottom.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number is marked by counting ticks from zero, up for plus and down for minus. Watch for students who put minus ten above minus seven because ten is bigger.

video_script.why: The child marks floors on a vertical line by counting ticks up or down from zero.
video_script.substitution: the book's own four floors marked on the floor line
video_script.anchor: the floor line of Ruhee, with four floors to mark
video_script.payoff_line: Count the ticks from zero, up for plus and down for minus.

final_answer.value: Mark −7, −4, +3, −10 on the vertical line (P = −7, Q = −4, R = +3, S = −10).
final_answer.spoken: plus three goes three ticks above zero, and minus four, minus seven and minus ten go four, seven and ten ticks below zero

names.Ruhee: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

hold_back: Answer: mark −7, −4, +3, −10 on the line (P = −7, Q = −4, R = +3, S = −10)
maths_rules: −4 is 4 ticks below 0; −7 is 7 ticks below 0.
Top to bottom the marks read +3, −4, −7, −10.
video_script.design: One idea: mark a floor by counting ticks from zero. One floor line throughout. Method as in the solved examples.
open_questions: The figure on the right was not visible: the video assumes unit ticks with zero marked on the line, as in the printed solution labels P, Q, R and S.
